newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia ICFI bank in $2 bln merger with Renaissance.
newsitem.headline: Russia ICFI bank in $2 bln merger with Renaissance.

text.p: Russian investment bank ICFI, a unit of the Uneximbank-MFK financial group, and investment bank Renaissance Capital are merging to form a new investment bank with total assets of over $2 billion, ICFI said on Wednesday.
"The total sum of assets of Bank MFK-Renaissance will be more than $2 billion, and the volume of funds under administration will be more than $1 billion," it said in a statement.

Vladimir Potanin will become chairman of the new bank's board. Potanin was Uneximbank president from 1993 to August 1996, when he was appointed First Deputy Prime Minister. He returned to Uneximbank in March after a cabinet reshuffle.
"This merger is taking place for the future development of the Russian capital market and will allow us to achieve world banking standards," Potanin said in the statement.
"It will allow us to attract investment not only for the companies with which Uneximbank is working but for other Russian companies."

Uneximbank, one of Russia's most powerful banks, has major stakes in strategic companies, including in the mining and energy sectors. ICFI said Renaissance had attracted nearly $4 billion in foreign investments of all kinds to the Russian economy.
